_about: Which generic course each British Flat course races on until it has its own build in the game (owner, 19 Nov 2026: 'these will form a stop gap meaning we can play any course we want'). Families from the course sheet's 'Generic courses' tab; the hand from the real course; the bigger or smaller stand side from the size of the course (owner, 19 Nov 17:39: 'a bigger (haydock, newcastle etc) and a smaller (pontefract, beverley)'). A race picks the generic course's start nearest its own distance (see 'starts'). Courses already built in full (Ascot, Newmarket's Rowley Mile and July Course, York) race on their own builds; the tier 1 and tier 2 builds (Goodwood, Epsom, Newbury, Doncaster, Chester, Sandown) are listed so they have a stand-in until their own build goes into the game.

generic.gen-tight-l-big: The Tight Track, left-handed, bigger stands
generic.gen-tight-l-small: The Tight Track, left-handed, smaller stands
generic.gen-tight-r-big: The Tight Track, right-handed, bigger stands
generic.gen-tight-r-small: The Tight Track, right-handed, smaller stands

generic.gen-hill-l-small: The Hill Track, left-handed, smaller stands
generic.gen-hill-r-big: The Hill Track, right-handed, bigger stands
generic.gen-hill-r-small: The Hill Track, right-handed, smaller stands

starts.note: every course of a kind has the same starts, both ways round and both sizes; a race takes the nearest start (e.g. 1m3f -> 1m4f, 1m5f -> 1m6f, 2m4f+ -> 2m on the Park, the longest); a real course's round sprints (Bath, Wetherby, Chester) can take the '6f (round)' start on the Tight Track if moved there

Carlisle.why: right-handed pear, against the collar over the last 4f

Catterick.why: small sharp left-handed oval with a sprint spur

Chepstow.why: left-handed oval with a straight mile (undulating)

Chester.why: tight, near-circular, left-handed (own build in progress)

Doncaster.why: galloping, straight mile, round-mile chute (own build in progress)

Epsom.why: left-handed, downhill turn into a cambered run-in (own build)

Ffos Las.why: flat left-handed oval with a straight 6f

Goodwood.why: right-handed, undulating, downhill sprint course (own build)

Newbury.why: galloping, straight mile (own build in progress)

Newcastle.why: left-handed, straight mile, all-weather, uphill finish

Nottingham.why: flat left-handed oval with a straight 6f

Redcar.why: long flat left-handed oval with a straight mile

Ripon.why: right-handed oval, cramped bends, a 6f straight

Yarmouth.why: long flat left-handed oval with a straight mile

overseas._about: Overseas courses on the existing generic courses (owner, 20 Nov 00:39-00:43: 'We don't need to create new ones if we have applicable ones'; 'We only need turf American for breeders cup'; 'a few French playing courses including longchamp and maybe Japan cup'; 'Meydan for Sheema classic'). All on the bigger stand side; metric trips take the nearest start (2400 m -> 1m4f, 2000 m -> 1m2f). Turf only.

ParisLongchamp (Arc).why: right-handed, a long downhill turn, undulating, a run-in of about 2.7f

Tokyo (Japan Cup).why: left-handed, big and galloping, a long straight rising to the post

Breeders' Cup (US turf races).why: the turf course inside a left-handed oval of about a mile, a short stretch; turf races only

Meydan (Dubai Sheema Classic).why: left-handed, big and galloping, a long straight, floodlit evening racing; the Sheema Classic's 2410 m takes the 1m4f start
